author: EmuCore - Hub
title: A New PS2 Emulator is in Development! A Promising Start!
summary: Video Game Esoterica evaluates Iris at alpha 0.1 as an independent PlayStation 2 emulator, using the limited proof-of-concept results to discuss why a second implementation matters even while PCSX2 remains dominant.

blocks.text: The ten-minute report is centered on an early project rather than a mature replacement. Iris is shown at alpha 0.1, where successful execution is evidence that its CPU, memory and graphics foundations are beginning to meet real software, not evidence of broad playability. An independent codebase can test different architectural choices, expose assumptions embedded in established emulators and provide another route for research. The creator’s framing values that diversity while acknowledging that PCSX2 is the practical default for most users.

An alpha demonstration ages quickly and may include hand-picked programs that avoid unimplemented hardware paths. Published metadata supplies no compatibility matrix, commit hash, automated test suite or performance measurements, so no percentage should be inferred from the footage. Check the project’s current repository, license and build instructions before experimenting, and expect regressions or missing features. The video is best preserved as a snapshot of emulator development beginning in public, not as a setup guide or a claim of parity with PCSX2.
